verdict.line: You lose if you trade into Darius's Apprehend before level 6 or let Hemorrhage stack past 3; you win by baiting E (Apprehend) into your E (Counter Strike) and running it back post-6.

brief.thesis: This is a near-even matchup (50.2% Jax win rate over 800 games) where the real edge sits in mechanics, not stats: Jax holds both the lane and solo-kill advantage because Counter Strike hard-answers Darius's core all-in tool, Apprehend. Whoever lands their disable first typically wins the exchange, and Darius's true-damage-heavy kit only closes that gap if he gets a free pull before you have E charged.

theirWindow.what: Darius wants to land Apprehend (E) into Crippling Strike (W) and Decimate (Q) edge before you hit 6. Don't stand in axe-pull range on cooldown-up trades; if he whiffs E, that's his all-in gone for ~14s and you can punish immediately.

yourWindow.what: Time Counter Strike (E) to start its channel right as the axe pull animates — dodge it, stun him, then Leap Strike (Q) in for a free empowered auto and follow-up trade before he can reset Hemorrhage stacks.

start.why: Run this on 68.6% of games (52.5% win rate, 686 games) — the extra AD and sustain directly offset Darius's true-damage-adjacent Crippling Strike and Hemorrhage bleed in early trades.

boots.why: Picked in 68.1% of games at 52.4% win rate — flat physical reduction blunts every auto and Q edge hit, which is where most of Darius's early damage comes from.

runes.keystoneWhy: This is the more common page (39% pick, 45.3% WR) and it rewards exactly what you want in this lane — stand-and-trade attack speed once you've dodged his Apprehend and committed to the fight.

summoners.why: Flash+Ignite is run in 83.4% of games (49.7% WR) — Ignite converts your solo-kill advantage into actual kills by cutting through his passive healing off Hemorrhage/W before he can reset with a takedown.

playing.title: Bait Apprehend before committing
playing.detail: Never enter auto-attack range on his E cooldown-up windows pre-6. Force him to throw the pull at a ward, a minion, or nothing — every whiffed Apprehend is a full trade cycle you get for free.

playing.title: Save E for his E, not for poke
playing.detail: Counter Strike's 2-second channel dodges Apprehend cleanly. Don't burn it on Decimate poke or to escape — the stun on a landed dodge is worth more than the block itself.

playing.title: Max W first, not Q
playing.detail: The data skill order (EQWWWR...) prioritizes W after an early Q point — take Q at 2 for the gap-close/reset, but pour points into W for trade damage rather than rushing Q max.

playing.title: Don't trade into 5 stacks
playing.detail: Track his Hemorrhage count visually on your own health bar tick. At 5 stacks his next W does bonus true-damage-adjacent execute-style damage — disengage or force his E first instead.

playing.title: All-in at level 6 on cooldown reads
playing.detail: Once Grandmaster's Might is up, look for any moment his E (Apprehend) is down. Leap Strike in, pop R, empowered auto — this is your highest-equity fight before item spikes even matter.

playing.title: Play around Trinity Force at 9+
playing.detail: This is your real power spike (49.5-53.5% WR core paths complete here). Start initiating trades you'd have avoided at level 4-5, since the empowered auto now closes the damage gap decisively.

playing.title: Hold Zhonya's for his ult, not yours
playing.detail: Once you have it, save the active for when he's stacked Noxian Guillotine resets and is threatening the execute — not as a generic panic button.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and all win-rate/pick-rate figures are pulled directly from measured OP.GG games on the current patch; the trade-pattern and timing analysis (Counter Strike vs Apprehend, stack thresholds, skill-order reasoning) is my own tactical read layered on top of that data.

stats.opponentTip: Use Counter Strike [E] when Darius uses Apprehend (E) to stun him and hit him before retreating with Leap Strike [Q]
